description: A genuine run of the real MatchWorkflow in which a deliberately invalid structured claim is vetoed by the Grounding step, the objection is routed back to the Explainer along the workflow's back edge, the corrected claim is verified, and the accepted overlay is produced. The trace is recorded from the run itself — never hand-authored. The fixture is a RECORDED TEST RUN on synthetic data: it must never be presented as a live incident.

degradations.description: Every degradation the run recorded. A valid fixture always has an empty list: any template fallback invalidates it.

fixture_format.description: Identifies this document as a grounding-recovery fixture.

fixture_version.description: Semver of this fixture instance. The file is versioned as recovery-example.v<major>.json; a major bump means a breaking schema change.

generated_at.description: When the generator ran, in UTC.

command.description: The exact command line that produced this fixture, so it can be reproduced.

attempt.description: The fault is only ever injected on the first attempt.

claimed_value.description: The value the injected claim stated.

metric.description: The metric whose value was perturbed.

true_value.description: The value the event log recomputes.

type.description: The fault kind: one metric value in the Explainer's first claim was moved beyond the grounding tolerance.

kind.description: Always 'recorded-test-run'. This fixture is a test run, never a live incident.

label.description: The human-readable honesty label. Any UI that shows this fixture must surface it verbatim.

correction_provider.description: The provider that served the retry which the Grounding step accepted. The showcase video may only use a fixture where this is 'Microsoft Foundry'.

explainer.description: Display label of the provider that served the Explainer (e.g. 'Microsoft Foundry' or 'Template engine').

template_fallback_used.description: Whether the deterministic template fallback claim was used anywhere in the run. The generator refuses to write the fixture when this is true.

acceptance.description: The Grounding step's verdict on the corrected claim: accepted=true (GroundingVerdict, JSON form).

corrected_claim.description: The Explainer's claim after the veto, written in answer to the objection (Explanation, JSON form).

invalid_claim.description: The Explainer's first claim for the target candidate, with the injected fault (touchline.models.claims.Explanation, JSON form).

overlay.description: The finished overlay produced from the accepted claim (touchline.models.overlay.Overlay, JSON form).

veto.description: The Grounding step's verdict on the invalid claim: accepted=false with the specific reasons (touchline.orchestration.grounding.GroundingVerdict, JSON form).

veto_trace_entry.description: The trace hand-off grounding→explainer with accepted=false — the objection routed back along the back edge (touchline.orchestration.handoffs.Handoff, JSON form).

revision.description: The git commit the code ran from (git rev-parse HEAD).

isolation.description: How the run stayed isolated from the live deployment.

match_minutes.description: How much of the synthetic match the run analysed.

target_candidate_id.description: The insight the fault was injected into.

trace.description: The hand-offs about the target candidate, in run order (touchline.orchestration.handoffs.Handoff, JSON form). The 'index' of each entry is its position in the run's full trace, so indices need not be contiguous here.

title: Grounding recovery example — recorded test run
